source.title: Primary School Curriculum Design — Agriculture, Grade 6
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (no pages param). ISBN 978-9914-43-005-9, First Published 2017, Revised 2024. Grade 6 is Upper Primary, NOT Junior School. Essence statement: 'Agriculture is an integrated learning area comprising aspects of agriculture and Home Science' — this is why the subject spans crop/soil/wildlife content alongside cooking, grooming, laundry and needlework. 4 strands / 10 sub-strands / 120 total suggested lessons. Written retroactively after the skill files already shipped (see CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md's standing rule to write this file BEFORE dispatching build agents next time) — transcribed from the same PDF read earlier in the session that produced web/src/skills/agricultureG6/.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Controlling Soil Erosion
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe types of soil erosion in the environment
Control soil erosion in the environment
Appreciate importance of conserving soil
keyInquiryQuestions: How does erosion control conserve the environment?
learningExperiences: Watch video clips or observe photographs or make field excursions to observe types of soil erosion
Demonstrate how to control various types of soil erosion (gulley, rill, splash and sheet erosion)
Discuss and make class presentations to appreciate the importance of controlling soil erosion to conserve soil in their environment
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — conservation of natural resources
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric's Exceeds tier for describing conservation asks for 'innovative ways' of conserving the resource, beyond just describing standard ways — matches the mandatory Evaluate-tier branch this competency requires.

subStrands.name: 1.2 Conserving Water — Sunken seedbed, Shallow pits
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify types of seedbeds that conserve soil moisture
Prepare different types of seedbeds that conserve soil moisture
Appreciate importance of conserving moisture in a seedbed to increase chances of plant growth
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we prepare a seedbed to conserve moisture?
learningExperiences: Watch video clips or observe photographs or visit sites to observe sunken bed and shallow pits
Prepare seedbeds that conserve moisture (sunken seedbed and shallow pit)
Utilise the sunken seedbed and shallow pits to appreciate the importance of soil moisture conservation in crop production
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Same shared strand rubric as 1.1/1.3 — 'describe innovative ways of conserving the resource' at Exceeds tier.
subStrands.notes: Split into two skill files per the Grade-6 'split into deeper skills' round — sunken seedbed and shallow pit are genuinely distinct construction techniques (one continuous trench-bed vs individual planting pockets).

subStrands.name: 1.3 Conserving Wild Animals
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify deterrents that can keep off wild animals from crop and domestic animals
Establish deterrents to keep off wild animals from destroying crops and domestic animals
Acknowledge the importance of deterrents in conserving wild animals
keyInquiryQuestions: How can wild animals be kept away from crops and domestic animals?
learningExperiences: Search for information on physical deterrents such as mesh fences, thorny fences, safe traps, innovative lights, innovative sounds, and deflectors
Select and establish a deterrent applicable in their local context
Discuss with a resource person the use of physical deterrents to acknowledge the importance of conserving wild animals in safeguarding crops and domestic animals
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Shared strand rubric — 'conserve three resources in the environment' at Exceeds tier for the strand overall (soil, water, wild animals).
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Protection of biodiversity against extinction (deterring animals without killing them)

subStrands.name: 2.1 Rearing Small Domestic Animals
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain routine practices in rearing of small domestic animals
Rear small domestic animals used as sources of food
Embrace the rearing of small domestic animals used as sources of food
keyInquiryQuestions: How does rearing of animals contribute to food production?
learningExperiences: Share experiences on routine practices in rearing of small domestic animals
Rear small domestic animal such as rabbits or guinea pigs to practise routine practices such as housing, feeding, watering, sanitation and parasite control
Make presentations to advocate the rearing of small domestic animals that are used for food
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — farming as a socio-economic activity
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand rubric: 'carry out five food production processes' at Exceeds tier (across all of 2.1-2.3 combined).

subStrands.name: 2.2 Preserving Crop Products — Fruits, Vegetables
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe how to preserve crop produce at home
Preserve crop produce using drying method
Adopt preservation of crop produce to reduce food wastage
keyInquiryQuestions: How does preservation of fruits and vegetables enhance food security?
learningExperiences: Watch video clips or listen to resource person and share experiences on how to preserve fruits and vegetables using sun-drying method
Preserve fruits or vegetables using sun-drying method
Utilize sun-drying method in preservation of fruits and vegetables at home to reduce food wastage
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology — parts of a plant (preserved produce parts)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand rubric shared across 2.1-2.3 — 'describe five food production processes' at Exceeds tier.

subStrands.name: 2.3 Cooking Food — Stewing, Baking (rubbing-in method)
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe different methods of cooking
Cook food using different methods
Embrace different methods of cooking in food production
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we cook foods by baking?
How can we cook foods by stewing?
learningExperiences: Watch video clips or observe demonstration on stewing and baking as methods of cooking
Cook foods using stewing and baking methods (rubbing-in method)
Serve foods prepared using stewing and baking methods
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — measuring ingredients for baking links to measurement of weights
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Safety of self and others while cooking food
subStrands.notes: Split into two skill files — stewing and baking are genuinely distinct cooking methods with distinct step sequences.

subStrands.name: 3.1 Good Grooming — Body cleaning
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe practices that enhance body cleanliness
Practice body cleanliness as a healthy habit
Recognise importance of body cleanliness as a hygienic practice
keyInquiryQuestions: How does body cleanliness enhance personal hygiene?
learningExperiences: Discuss and share experiences on practices that enhance body cleanliness (managing sweat, acnes and pimples, menstrual hygiene and care of pubic parts) for personal hygiene
Embrace applicable good routines that suit their body cleanliness
Discuss the importance of body cleanliness as a hygienic habit
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology — growth and development
scopeNotes: include: managing sweat, acne/pimples, menstrual hygiene, and care of pubic parts — all four named explicitly in the source parenthetical, handled with factual/dignified/non-graphic framing in the shipped skill, per KICD's own textbook register
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand rubric: 'applies two hygiene practices (body cleanliness and stain removal)' at Exceeds tier for the strand overall.
subStrands.notes: Kept as a single skill file with no visual by design (personal-hygiene content, not diagram-based) and 4 QuestionKinds rather than 5 (no genuine sequence/spatial/numeric angle) — both deliberate, documented in the skill file's own code comment.

subStrands.name: 3.2 Laundry: Stain Removal
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify common stains on clothing and household articles
Remove common stains from clothing and household articles
Adopt stain removal for personal hygiene
keyInquiryQuestions: How does stain removal enhance personal hygiene?
learningExperiences: Use digital resources and sample articles to identify common stains (blood and grass) on clothing and household articles
Carry out removal of common stains (blood and grass) on clothing and household articles
Practise and adopt stain removal for personal hygiene
scopeNotes: include: blood and grass are the only two stain types named — other stains may appear only as clearly-labelled wrong-answer distractors, never as core content
subStrands.notes: Split into two skill files — identifying vs removing are different cognitive tasks, and blood (protein-based, cold-water treatment) vs grass (pigment-based, detergent treatment) genuinely need different removal methods.

subStrands.name: 4.1 Crocheting Stitches
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify crocheting stitches in making household articles
Use crocheting stitches to make a household articles
Adopt the use of crocheting stiches in making household articles
keyInquiryQuestions: How can crocheting reduce the cost of purchasing household articles?
learningExperiences: Observe a demonstration by resource person, photographs, or watch video clip to identify crocheting stitches (single and double crochet stitches) in making household article
Use (single or double crochet stitches) to make articles such as mats, cleaning rug, and surface wipers
Construct articles using crocheting stitches and showcase the household articles to promote adoption in their daily routines
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand rubric: 'identify requirements, assemble the requirements, construct the item and produce usable finished product' at Exceeds tier.
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Financial literacy (learners save costs by constructing usable household articles using crocheting skills)
subStrands.notes: Largest single sub-strand in the whole design (16 lessons). Split into two skill files — stitch identification/technique vs the three named articles, with the financial-literacy PCI given its own numeric cost-comparison branch in the articles skill.

subStrands.name: 4.2 Constructing Moist Bed Garden
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the meaning of moist bed garden
Construct a moist bed garden for growing a selected crop
Embrace the use of moist bed garden in growing crops
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we construct a moist bed garden to grow crops?
learningExperiences: Search and share information on the meaning of moist bed garden
Construct a moist bed (sunken or raised moist bed) using locally available materials
Establish and grow a crop of their choice to embrace the use of moist bed garden
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand rubric shared with 4.1 — same production-techniques rubric.
subStrands.notes: Split into two skill files — sunken (traps water below grade, best for dry sites) and raised (improves drainage/aeration, best for waterlogged-prone sites) are opposite mechanisms, not relabeled text. Core competency here is collaboration-flavored rather than 'critical thinking', so per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md these two skills can legitimately stay lighter on mandatory Analyze/Evaluate branches (though each still has one).
